text:
Anita: Running into a flaky RuntimeError when our async SDK client is created at module import in a FastAPI app with uvicorn --reload. Repro below. Anyone recognize the pattern?

Anita: ```py
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()
client = AsyncClient(api_key="test")  # module-scope init

async def heartbeat():
    while True:
        await client.generate("ping")
        await asyncio.sleep(2)

@app.on_event('startup')
async def start():
    asyncio.create_task(heartbeat())

@app.get('/')
async def home():
    return {'ok': True}

# uvicorn app:app --reload
```

Anita: On code reload I sometimes see:```
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 247, in __enter__
    self._loop.run_until_complete(self.__aenter__())
```

Mike: That stacktrace smells like something in the SDK is using a sync context manager path that ends up calling asyncio.run(). Creating AsyncClient at import time might trigger a sync shim.

Sarah: We had a similar bug in a different library where auth refresh used anyio.run() from sync code. If the SDK tries to warm up a background task during __init__, it can race with uvicorn's loop.

Anita: I verified moving client creation into the startup event fixes it:```py
@app.on_event('startup')
async def start():
    global client
    client = AsyncClient(api_key='test')
    await client.__aenter__()
    asyncio.create_task(heartbeat())
```
But we shouldn't force everyone to do that.

Tom: Two fixes: (1) SDK should not call asyncio.run() in any path reachable from import/sync code. (2) Delay spawning background tasks until there is an active loop (defer until first await or provide explicit start()).

Mike: Agreed. Also the SDK could detect no-running-loop and raise a clear error: "AsyncClient must be created inside an async event loop or use AsyncClient.defer_start=True". Better than bubbling up asyncio.run runtime errors.

Sarah: Another related issue: sharing one AsyncClient across multiple uvicorn workers/threads triggered httpx LocalProtocolError in our tests. We should document thread/worker safety and recommend per-process clients.

Anita: I've opened a minimal repro and will link it in the SDK issue. Adding a temporary note to the developer quickstart: avoid module-level AsyncClient init.

ci-bot: Created issue redwood/redwood-python-sdk#433 - "AsyncClient: module-level init causes asyncio.run() RuntimeError on uvicorn reload" (https://github.com/redwood/redwood-python-sdk/issues/433)

Mike: For a short-term patch we can: - remove any asyncio.run/anyio.run usage from AsyncClient.__init__ - add deferred_init flag - provide async init method (await client.start()) - add a helpful error message when init attempted without loop.

Tom: We should also add an integration test: launch uvicorn with --reload in CI matrix and import an example app that does module-scope init to catch regressions (may be flaky, but useful on main branch).

Sarah: Docs snippet to include in onboarding:```py
# recommended pattern for FastAPI
app = FastAPI()
client = None

@app.on_event('startup')
async def startup():
    global client
    client = AsyncClient(api_key='...')
    await client.__aenter__()

@app.on_event('shutdown')
async def shutdown():
    await client.aclose()
```

Anita: I'll prepare the PR to change the init behavior and add the doc note. Ping me if you want to review. :+1:

Mike: I'll review the patch and help add the uvicorn reload test.

Tom: I'll update the CHANGELOG and add the feature request for a `start()` helper and clearer error strings.

Anita: Thanks everyone — temporary doc added, PR incoming.
